newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Ingersoll sidelines FKI in N.Tonks bid.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Ingersoll sidelines FKI in N.Tonks bid.

text.p: U.S.-based Ingersoll-Rand Co on Monday launched a surprise agreed cash offer for British building products group Newman Tonks Group valuing the firm at around 230 million pounds ($376 million).
Ingersoll's offer, at 175 pence a share, sidelined a hostile bid offer from British engineering group FKI Plc which had valued Newman at 195.7 million pounds.
Newman's board had rejected FKI's offer but gave its unanimous backing to Ingersoll's bid, saying it represented a 28 percent premium over the FKI's "unsolicited and hostile offer".
The offer by Ingersoll, a multinational manufacturer of industrial machinery, was welcomed by investors, and Newman shares surged by 28 pence, or 18.5 percent, to 179-1/2 pence.
The share outperformed the FTSE all share building materials sector by 2.63 percent.
Newman directors have already accepted the Ingersoll offer in respect of 1.2 million shares representing 0.9 percent of the issued share capital.
Ingersoll-Rand's vice president Brian Jellison said Newman Tonks would help the architectural hardware group to shape its European strategy.
"It will serve us better in the fast-growing Asian markets as well," Jellison told Reuters.
Newman's exports, both direct and indirect, form almost 20 percent of its total turnover.

Newman also forecast profits before tax, exceptional items and bid costs of not less than 18 million pounds for the year to December 31, 1996. Earnings per share, before exceptional items and bid costs, were forecast at 8.75 pence per share.
The company said it expected to pay a dividend of 4.4 pence.
Newman's 1995 pretax profit stood at 27.2 million pounds.
According to Reuters Securities 3000 data, a consensus of seven estimates pegged Newman's 1996 pretax profit at 15.8 million pounds, rising to 20 million stg in 1997.
The data cites Newman's current operating margin at 6.95 percent with return on equity of 27.03 percent.
Jellison did not make a commitment to retain all of Newman's 4,500 employees but said the acquisition would "see job creations".
Jellison said the group was due to announce its 1996 results on Monday and was expecting a 15 percent growth, its average for the last three years.
Separately, FKI said it had acceptances for its offer of some 20.6 percent of Newman Tonks shares, and said it owned or had agreed to buy further shares totalling 0.4 percent.
FKI's offer, which was scheduled to close on February 7, had been accepted by fund management groups M&G and Britannic Assurance, who control some 13.37 percent of Newman Tonks shares.
None of them was immediately available for comment. ($1=.6119 Pound)
